To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) severe JPEG and JPEG2002 image compression of iris images can be performed with minimal impact on iris recognition performance, and (2) the resulting compressed iris image files can be as small as 2000 to 4000 bytes.

(1) it is possible to severely compress iris images and yet achieve very good recognition performance; (2) it is possible for an iris algorithm to be tolerant to severe compression; (3) the compression algorithms that are best at retaining the information needed for iris recognition are JPEG and JPEG2001.

(i) the compression of iris images to 2000 bytes is feasible without a significant impact on recognition performance, (ii) the IrisCode templates generated from such compressed images are only slightly changed, (iii) the error rate is only slightly increased by such compression, and (iv) the entropy per code bits is increased only marginally by such compression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reducing the amount of data needed to store iris images while retaining recognition performance.
the problem of how to reduce iris image size for transmission and storage, without compromising performance.
the question: How much image data size reduction is possible with minimal loss of recognition performance?

severe compression of the image data does not affect the performance of the IrisCode algorithms, and that the image data could be stored and transmitted as JPEG or JPEG2000 images at 1/300 of the current data rate.
severe image compression has a negligible impact on the recognition performance of iris algorithms.
the impact of severe compression on recognition performance is negligible.

the compression schemes we present are practical and effective, and that they should be considered for implementation in the field.
it is possible today, using JPEG and JPEG20000 compression schemes, to store and transmit iris images with minimal loss in recognition performance.

it is possible, with careful design of compression algorithms, to compress iris images severely while retaining good recognition performance.
the use of JPEG and JPEG20001 compression at high quality levels is a viable alternative to the current standard of storing IrisCode templates for database search.

the current generation of iris algorithms can tolerate a very high level of image compression and that this is likely to continue to hold for future generations as well, as long as image compression is applied only to the iris region.
